translations.text: After Israel had been taken captive and Jerusalem had become desolate, Jeremiah sat down and wept and sang this lament over Jerusalem, saying: How the city once full of people sits alone! She has become like a widow. She who was great among the nations, who ruled over the provinces, has become a payer of tribute.
She wept bitterly in the night, and her tears flowed down her cheeks. Among all those who love her, there is no one to comfort her. All who love her have betrayed her; they have become her enemies.
Judah was taken away because of her great humiliation and her heavy slavery. She settled among the nations but found no rest. All who pursued her caught her in the midst of those who oppressed her.
The roads to Zion mourn because no one comes to the festival. All her gates are ruined. Her priests groan. Her young women have been taken captive, and she herself is angry within.
Those who oppress her have become her masters. Her enemies rejoice because the Lord has humbled her for her many acts of wrongdoing. Her little children have gone into captivity before her oppressor.
All her beauty has been taken away from the daughter of Zion. Her rulers have become like deer that find no pasture. They walk without strength before the one pursuing them.

Jerusalem remembered the days of her humiliation and disobedience, and all the possessions she loved that were hers in earlier days. When her people fell into the hands of her oppressor, there was no one to help her. When her enemies saw her like this, they laughed at the displacement that had overtaken her.
Jerusalem sinned grievously; because of this she was shaken. All who honored her have humiliated her, for they have seen her nakedness. She herself groaned and turned back.

Her uncleanness is beneath her feet. She did not remember her end, and she brought her great glory low. There is no one to comfort her. Look, Lord, at my humiliation, for my enemy has exalted himself.
Her oppressor stretched out his hand over all her treasured possessions. For she saw the nations enter her holy place—those whom you had commanded not to enter your assembly.
All her people groan as they search for bread. They have traded all her precious possessions for food to restore their lives. Look, Lord, and take notice, for she has become despised.

All of you traveling along the road to your destinations, turn and see whether there is any suffering like the suffering that has come upon me. The Lord opened his mouth against me and humbled me on the day of his fierce anger.
He sent fire from his heights and brought it down upon my bones. He spread a net for my feet and turned me back. He brought me to ruin, leaving me in anguish all day long.

They made me keep watch over wrongdoing. These acts became tangled in my hands and rose upon my neck. My strength grew weak, for the Lord placed anguish in my hands. I cannot find the strength to stand.
The Lord removed all my mighty men from my midst. He called for a time against me to crush my chosen men. The Lord trod a winepress for the virgin daughter of Judah. For these things I will weep.
My eye poured out tears because the one who comforts me, who restores my soul, has gone far away from me. My children have been ruined because my enemy has prevailed over me.

Zion stretched out her hands, but there is no one to comfort her. The Lord gave a command concerning Jacob: those who oppress him surround him. Jerusalem has become like a menstruating woman among them.
The Lord is righteous, because [?] defied his word. Listen, all peoples, and see my suffering. My young women and young men have gone into captivity.
I called to my loved ones, but they deceived me. My priests and elders perished in the city, for [?] searched for food to restore their lives, but they did not find any.

Look, Lord, for I am distressed. My insides are in turmoil, and my heart has turned over within me, for I was fiercely angry. Outside, the sword has left me childless, like the death that occurs inside a house.

Listen now, for I am groaning, and there is no one to comfort me. All my enemies heard of my troubles and rejoiced, because you are the one who did these things to me. You brought a day upon me and called for a time; they became like me.
Let all their wickedness come before you, and afflict them as they afflicted me because of all my sins. For my groans are many, and my heart is sorrowful.
How the Lord has crushed the daughter of Zion in his anger! He has thrown the glory of Israel down from heaven to earth and has not remembered his footstool on the day of his anger.

The Lord swallowed up the daughter of Zion without pity. He demolished all the beautiful things of Jacob in his wrath. He brought the lofty places of the daughter of Judah level with the ground. He despised her king and her rulers.
He has shattered all the horns of Israel in his fierce anger. He has drawn back his right hand before the enemy. He has made a flame blaze like a fire in Jacob and has consumed everything around him.
He drew his bow like an enemy and made his right hand strong like an adversary. He killed all my loved ones. He poured out his anger like fire in the tent of the daughter of Zion.
The Lord has become like an enemy. He has engulfed Israel; he has engulfed its multitudes and destroyed its fortified places. He has increased the humiliation and abasement of the daughter of Judah.
He spread out his dwelling like a grapevine and destroyed his festival. The Lord made Zion forget festival and Sabbath. In his fierce anger he brought disgrace upon king, priest, and ruler.
The Lord abandoned his altar and cast away his sanctuary. He handed the wall of her multitudes over to the enemy. They raised their voices in the Lord’s house as on a festival day.

The Lord considered and resolved to destroy the wall of the daughter of Zion. He stretched a measuring line over her and did not draw his hand back from consuming her. The outer rampart mourned, and the wall weakened along with it.
Her gates became level with the ground. They destroyed her bars, and he crushed her king and her rulers among the nations. She has no law, and her prophets have seen no vision from the Lord.
The elders of the daughter of Zion sat on the ground in silence. They scattered dust on their heads and wrapped themselves in sackcloth. The chosen virgins of Jerusalem fell down to the ground.

My eyes failed with tears, my heart was troubled, and my glory poured out upon the ground because of the destruction of the daughter of my people, as little children and nursing infants collapsed in the city’s streets.
They said to their mothers, “Where are grain and wine?” as they grew faint like wounded people in the city streets, as they poured out their lives into their mothers’ laps.

What shall I bear witness to, or to whom shall I compare you, daughter of Jerusalem? Who will save you, or who will plead for you, virgin daughter of Zion? For the cup of destruction has grown great. Who will heal you?
Your prophets saw empty things and foolishness. They covered up your wrongdoing instead of reversing your captivity. They saw and brought you empty and rejected oracles.

Everyone passing along the road clapped their hands at you. They hissed and shook their heads at the daughter of Jerusalem, saying, “Is this the city that is the crown of glory, the joy of the whole earth?”

All your enemies opened their mouths against you. They hissed and ground their teeth, saying, “We have swallowed her up! Indeed, this is the day we were waiting for. We have found her and have feasted our eyes on her.”

The Lord did what he had planned. He fulfilled the words he had commanded from his earliest days. He demolished without pity. He made your enemy rejoice over you and raised the horn of the one who oppresses you.
Their heart cried out to the Lord. Walls of Zion, pour down tears like a torrent day and night. Give yourself no rest, daughter; do not let your eye be still.

Rise and pray in the night, at the beginning of your watches. Pour out your heart like water before the Lord. Lift your hands to him for the lives of your little children, who have fainted from hunger at the head of every street.

Look, Lord, and take notice: who is it that has afflicted him? Will women eat the fruit of their wombs like this? The cook has inflicted suffering. Will they kill little children nursing at the breast? Or will you kill a priest and a prophet in the Lord’s sanctuary?
The young children and the old lay in the street. The virgins and the young men went into captivity. You killed them with a sword on the day of your anger; you slaughtered them without sparing them.
You called for a feast day around my dwelling, and no one escaped or survived on the day of the Lord’s anger, as you seized and multiplied all my enemies.
I am the man who sees affliction. He came down upon me with the rod of his anger.
He seized me and led me into darkness, not into light.
Indeed, he turned his hand against me all day long.
He made my flesh and my skin grow old; he broke my bones.
He built a wall around me and hemmed in my head.
He humbled me in dark places; he made me sit like those who have been dead forever.
He built a wall around me, and I cannot get out. He increased my bronze fetters.
Even when I cry out to him and call aloud, he does not allow my prayer to pass through.
He walled off my roads and blocked my paths. It was stirred up—
a bear lying in wait. He became a lion against me in a hidden place.
He pursued the one who stood firm and struck me; he left me ruined.
He drew his bow and set me up as a target to shoot his arrow into me.
He made the arrows from his quiver pass into my kidneys.
I became a laughingstock to all the people; I was their song all day long.
He filled me with bitterness and made me drunk with gall.
He ground my teeth with gravel and fed me ashes.
He has cast my soul away from peace. I have forgotten my good things.
My strength and my hope perished because of the Lord.
I remembered, out of my affliction and my persecution, bitterness and gall.
They will remember me, and my soul is bowed down within me.
I will put this in my heart; because of this I will wait patiently.
For the Lord’s mercy, because he has not abandoned me, nor has his compassion failed in the evenings and throughout all the days.
Have mercy on us, Lord, for we have not come to an end, because your compassion has not failed. It will be new in the morning. Great is your faithfulness.
My soul said, “The Lord is my portion; because of this I will wait patiently for him.”
The Lord is good to those who wait for him. He is good to the soul that seeks him.
And it will patiently wait for the Lord’s salvation and remain quiet.
It is good for a person to take the yoke upon himself in his youth.
He will sit alone and be silent, because he has taken it upon himself.
He will turn his cheek toward the one who strikes him; he will have his fill of insults.
For the Lord will not abandon him forever.
Because he humbled them, he will have compassion on him according to the abundance of his mercy.
For he did not respond from his heart; he humbled human beings.
To humble beneath his feet all the prisoners of the earth,
to turn aside a person’s justice before the face of the Most High,
to wrong a person when he is judged—the Lord did not say this.
Who said this and had it happen when the Lord had not commanded these things?
Evil and good do not come from the mouth of the Most High.
Why should a person complain about his sin while that person is alive?
Let us examine our ways and investigate our conduct, and let us return to the Lord.
Let us lift our hearts upon our hands before the Most High, who is in heaven.
We sinned, we acted wickedly, and we provoked anger, but you did not forgive us.
You spread out [?] and made an end in anger. You pursued us and killed us; you did not spare us.
You spread out a cloud for yourself because of my prayer,
so that I would be humbled and not see, and to cast me out. You placed us among the nations.
All our enemies opened their mouths against us.
Fear and anger came upon us; they carried us off and struck us.
My eye will pour out streams of water over the destruction of the daughter of my people,
My eye is in pain. I will not be silent or lift my head.
until the Lord looks down and sees from heaven.
My eye will bring pain to my soul more than all the daughters of the city.
My enemies hunted me down like a bird, for no reason.
They put me to death in a pit and laid a stone over me.
Water poured over my head. I said, “He has abandoned me.”
I called upon your name, Lord, from a pit down below.
You heard my voice; do not close your ears to my plea.
You came near to help me on the day I called on you. You said to me, “Do not be afraid.”
You pleaded my soul’s cases, Lord; you redeemed my life.
You saw my troubles, Lord; you judged my case.
You saw all their vengeance and all their schemes against me.
You have heard their insults, Lord, and all the schemes they devised against me throughout the day.
And the movement of the lips of those who rise up against me, and their meditations, were against me all day long.
Their sitting down and their getting up—look at their eyes.
You will repay them, Lord, according to the deeds of their hands.
You yourself will repay them with suffering for the strength of their hearts.
You will pursue them in your anger and destroy them from beneath heaven, Lord.
How the gold has grown dark, and the fine silver has changed! The holy stones have been scattered at the head of every street.
The precious children of Zion, valued in gold—how they have been compared to clay vessels, the work of a potter’s hands!
Dragons have uncovered their breasts and nursed their young. But the daughters of my people have become like an ostrich in the desert, with no one to have mercy on them.
The nursing infant’s tongue has stuck to its throat from thirst. The little children asked for bread, but there was no one to break it for them.
Those who ate delicacies have perished in the streets, and those who were brought up on scarlet have clothed themselves in dung.
The lawlessness of the daughter of my people has grown greater than the lawlessness of Sodom, which was overthrown in an instant, without anyone wearing out their hands against it.
Her Nazirites, who were set apart, were pure. They were whiter than snow and brighter than milk; their appearance was finer than a sapphire.
Their appearance has grown darker than a shadow. They were not recognized in the streets. Their skin has stuck to their bones; they have dried up and become like wood.
Those killed by the sword are better off than those killed by famine, for they went about pierced by hunger for bread and the food of the fields.
The hands of compassionate women cooked their own children. They became food for them during the destruction of the daughter of my people.
The Lord has fully carried out his wrath; he has poured out the fury of his anger. He kindled a fire in Zion, and it consumed her foundations.
The kings of the earth and everyone living in the inhabited world did not believe that the enemy and the oppressor would enter through the gates of Jerusalem.
It was because of the sins of her prophets and the injustices of her priests, who shed righteous blood in her midst.
Those who guarded her wandered through the streets; they were stained with blood. In their helplessness, they touched their clothes.

“Keep away, you unclean people!” Say to them, “Keep away! Keep away! Do not touch them!” For they caught fire and wandered. Say among the nations, “They will no longer continue to stay in the dwelling place.”
The face of the Lord is their portion. He will no longer look upon them. They did not respect the priests or show mercy to the elders.
While we were still alive, our eyes failed as we looked for help. What we were looking to was useless. We looked to a nation that would not save us.
We guarded our little children to keep them from walking in our streets. Our time drew near, our days were completed, and our appointed time came.
Those pursuing us became swifter than the eagles of the sky. They swarmed over the mountains and set ambushes for us in the wilderness.
The breath of our face is Christ the Lord. He was captured in their acts of destruction. Of him they said, “In his shadow we will be safe among the nations.”
Rejoice and be glad, daughter of Idumea, who lives upon the land. For the Lord’s cup is coming upon you too. You will become drunk and pour yourself out.
Your lawlessness has come to an end, daughter of Zion. He will no longer deport you. He has punished your lawlessness, daughter of Edom; he has exposed your wickedness.
Remember, Lord, what has happened to us. Look and see our disgrace.
Our inheritance has passed to foreigners. Our houses have become the property of strangers.
We have become orphans, with no father left to us. Our mothers have become like widows.
In our days, we drink our water for money, and our wood comes at a price.
They came upon our necks and pursued us. We grew weary and found no rest.
Egypt gave a hand to Assyria as they ate their fill of bread.
Our fathers sinned and are no longer here, but we have borne their lawlessness.
Slaves have become our masters. There is no one to rescue us from their hands.
At the risk of our lives, we will bring in our bread in the face of the sword of the wilderness.
Our skin became black like an oven. They were drawn down together before the winds of famine.
They violated the women in Zion; they violated the virgins in the cities of Judah.
They hung the rulers up by their hands. They showed no respect for the elders.
The chosen men sat and wept. They ground grain at the mill, and the boys grew weak under bundles of wood.
The elders ceased gathering at the gates. The chosen men stopped singing their songs.
The joy of our heart has failed. Our dancing has turned into mourning.
The crown has fallen from our head. Woe to us, because we have sinned!
Because of this, our heart has become distressed. Because of this, our eyes have grown dark.
Because Mount Zion has been destroyed, foxes walk upon it.
But you, Lord, remain forever. Your throne endures from generation to generation.
Why will you forget us while we are being humiliated and abandon us for many days?
Turn us back to you, Lord, and we will return. Renew our days as they were before.
For you have utterly abandoned us and have been very angry with us.
